reason: E2 supports that grain size and phase boundaries affect domain-wall movement and coercivity in AlCoCrFeNi-type alloys, but none of the cited evidence addresses local strain fields, magnetocaloric effect, or heat conduction in this system. E1 and E3 are about different alloy systems and unrelated properties, providing no support for the key premises.
premises: Ultrafine grains increase grain boundary density in AlCoCrFeNi
Higher grain boundary density enhances local strain fields
Enhanced local strain fields facilitate easier magnetic domain wall motion
Easier domain wall motion reduces coercivity and hysteresis
High interface density aids rapid heat conduction
